claims.text: SSRIs and SNRIs can cause hyponatremia.
claims.quote: Hyponatremia may occur as a result of treatment with SNRIs and SSRIs, including ZOLOFT.

claims.text: Sodium below 110 mmol/L has been reported.
claims.quote: Cases with serum sodium lower than 110 mmol/L have been reported.

claims.text: In many cases the cause appears to be SIADH.
claims.quote: In many cases, this hyponatremia appears to be the result of the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH).

claims.text: Symptoms: headache, trouble concentrating, memory impairment, confusion, weakness and unsteadiness that can lead to falls.
claims.quote: Signs and symptoms of hyponatremia include headache, difficulty concentrating, memory impairment, confusion, weakness, and unsteadiness, which may lead to falls.

claims.text: Higher risk: older adults, patients on diuretics, and volume-depleted patients.
claims.quote: Elderly patients, patients taking diuretics, and those who are volume-depleted may be at greater risk of developing hyponatremia with SSRIs and SNRIs

claims.text: With symptomatic hyponatremia, stop the drug and treat.
claims.quote: In patients with symptomatic hyponatremia, discontinue ZOLOFT and institute appropriate medical intervention.
